verification.reason: The accumulation is real. `retire` loops over every `seen` folder and calls `holdsStray` with the store-lifetime `this.#judged` map (git-record-store.ts:73, 269-276). Each fresh entry is stored there as a parsed `SharedRecord` or `Cell` (state-tree.ts:249-252), and nothing evicts entries. The per-folder checks (entry count, record size, `total > tipLimit`) bound only one folder at a time. No check bounds the total across the folders of one call, so a tip with many folders can add up to far more than `tipLimit` of parsed records. The decision text says retirement "works on a tip past any limit" (line 52), and the code does not enforce that for memory. I could not run it. Whether the heap actually runs out depends on how large the parsed objects are and on Node's heap limit. The retained data is parsed objects, not the raw bytes, which the loop frees after each folder, so the "eight times `tipLimit`" figure is an estimate. The caller is also not built yet. The scheduled job is a later pull request, so it may batch its `seen` map. A run that retires a multi-GiB tip in one call would settle it.

evidence.snippet: - `dispose` first writes a disposal mark to the cell, and `add` refuses a changeset whose cell holds one. Disposal is permanent: the port has no way to recreate a changeset, since one would need an incarnation every record and writer carries.

`GitRecordStore.retire(seen)` takes changeset names, each with the tree ID its folder had when the caller decided. In one commit it removes each folder whole, cell included, with no mark. A retired changeset is the same as one never written, so a reopened pull request records again from nothing. Retiring a disposed changeset takes its mark too, so a retirement undoes a disposal. That is wanted: a retirement leaves the tip as if the pull request never recorded, and a disposal's purpose, removing a changeset's records from the tip for good, holds once the job has retired it.

verification.reason: Base rule 3 of the shared-record decision (line 107) says "Disposal is permanent: the port has no way to recreate a changeset, since one would need an incarnation every record and writer carries." The head's `retire` removes a disposed changeset's folder whole, mark included (state-tree.ts `disposed` reads the mark from the cell, which retirement deletes). `withoutFolders` drops the whole folder and `removesOnly` checks only that entries disappear. The new decision (line 32) and the test at retire.test.ts:592-599 say outright that a retirement undoes a disposal, and the test shows `add` failing with `disposed` before `retire` and succeeding after it. So a changeset that was disposed can be written again, with no incarnation carried by records or writers. The new decision amends only rule 13's retention and the git store's limit refusal. It never amends the "Disposal is permanent" clause, and head text cannot excuse the departure. The base reason still holds. A stale host that adds old records after retirement, or relays a post with a higher lease generation into a cell that restarted, meets no guard. I did not trace the lease-generation restart through the code, because it lives outside state-git/src. The disposed-changeset path is traced and is enough.
